item.title: White House shooting: Who is Rahmanullah Lakanwal? Afghan national named suspect in security breach
item.description: An Afghan national, identified as Rahmanullah Lakanwal, is accused of critically injuring two National Guard members near the White House. The suspect, who entered the U.S. in 2021, allegedly fired a handgun at the soldiers during a patrol. The FBI is investigating the incident as a possible act of terrorism.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Last criminal case against Trump dismissed; name cleared in 2020 US elections interference case
item.description: A Georgia judge has dismissed the final criminal case against Donald Trump concerning the 2020 election, impacting co-defendants like Rudy Giuliani. This move ends all state-level charges, with prosecutors citing election challenges not being a crime and federal jurisdiction as key reasons. Trump's legal team hailed the decision as political, following earlier setbacks for the prosecution.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UK PM Keir Starmer does the ‘6-7’ meme, gets schooled by teacher
item.description: During a visit to Welland Academy, Prime Minister Keir Starmer was playfully drawn into the banned "6-7" meme by schoolchildren. Despite a teacher's reminder of the rule, Starmer joined the gesture, leading to laughter and a humorous social media post about potential detention. The lighthearted moment overshadowed the visit's original purpose of promoting free school meals and tackling child poverty.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Candace Owens puts her show off air after she claims Emmanuel Macron tried to harm her and was tied to Charlie Kirk’s death
item.description: Candace Owens has halted her show, alleging French President Macron plotted her assassination, a claim she reported to the White House and US counterterrorism teams. She also implicated the Macrons in Charlie Kirk's death. These accusations surface amidst a defamation lawsuit filed by the Macrons against Owens for her claims about Brigitte Macron's gender identity.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Who is the Burnt Peanut? The 3D peanut avatar behind Twitch’s 2025 breakout success
item.description: A streamer known as The Burnt Peanut has achieved remarkable success on Twitch in 2025, experiencing an 80% follower surge in November. His unique blend of high-energy FPS gameplay, a distinctive 3D peanut avatar, and relatable streaming style has propelled him to stardom. This reinvention, born from burnout, has captivated audiences and solidified his position as a breakout personality.

item.title: “I’d rather be a rich socialist than a broke boy defending capitalism”: Hasan Piker fires back at critics
item.description: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker defended his wealthy lifestyle amid accusations of hypocrisy for supporting socialist ideals. He declared, “I’d rather be a rich socialist than a broke boy defending capitalism,” asserting that personal success doesn't invalidate systemic critique. Piker argues his income from the platform and advocacy for left-leaning causes demonstrate his commitment to change, not personal poverty.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Shooting near White House: Two National Guard soldiers shot, President Trump briefed
item.description: Two National Guard soldiers were critically wounded in a shooting near the White House. President Trump issued a statement condemning the "animal" responsible and vowing a steep price, while also praising the military. The suspect is in custody, and authorities are responding to the scene.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who is Carl Westcott? The 85-year-old disabled army veteran Katy Perry is seeking $5 million from
item.description: In a surprising turn of events, pop sensation Katy Perry is facing backlash after attempting to claim nearly $5 million from 85-year-old veteran Carl Westcott over a property disagreement. Westcott, who sold his land to Perry and Orlando Bloom back in 2020, alleges that he was under medication during the contract signing.
item.dc:creator: TOI Trending Desk

item.title: Once MacKenzie Scott borrowed $1,000 from her friend to pay college fees, now the billionaire is returning the favour
item.description: Billionaire philanthropist MacKenzie Scott, once saved from college dropout by a friend's loan, is now a major backer of her former roommate's student-lending startup. This venture aids low-income students lacking co-signers, mirroring Scott's own past vulnerability. Her massive, unrestricted donations champion educational access and equity, demonstrating a profound return of kindness.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: SteveWillDoIt sparks controversy by calling Mike Majlak the biggest loser ever after heated Logan Paul podcast moment
item.description: YouTuber SteveWillDoIt clashed with Mike Majlak on Logan Paul's podcast. The interview turned sour, leading Steve to walk off. He later posted on Instagram calling Majlak a 'loser'. The incident gained significant social media attention. Logan Paul expressed surprise at Steve's behavior. Majlak and Paul have not yet responded to Steve's posts.

item.title: Democrats have no solution to fix education: Vivek Ramaswamy attacks Ohio governor candidate
item.description: Republican Vivek Ramaswamy is highlighting education in Ohio's gubernatorial race, accusing former health director Amy Acton of worsening inequality through COVID-19 school closures. Ramaswamy argues these lockdowns caused irreversible learning losses, particularly for disadvantaged students, and criticizes Democrats for lacking solutions to fix education.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Jet rides for girlfriend, SWAT deployments, and Shein deals: Top 5 controversies of FBI Director Kash Patel
item.description: Kash Patel's time as FBI chief during the Trump administration stirred considerable debate. Among the claims were allegations of misusing government aircraft for personal jaunts to visit his girlfriend, controversial decisions regarding the handling of Jeffrey Epstein's case, and the dismissal of senior FBI personnel.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: What led to YouTube giving EricOneHive three copyright strikes and why is he ready to quit Clash of Clans completely?
item.description: YouTuber EricOneHive faces potential channel deletion within seven days due to three copyright strikes from Supercell, the makers of Clash of Clans. Despite efforts to counterclaim, he vows to cease all Supercell game content, even if his channel is saved. Fans express support, lamenting the potential loss to the gaming community.

item.title: Gunshots heard near Guinea-Bissau presidential palace; 4 coups since 1973
item.description: Gunfire erupted outside Guinea-Bissau's presidential palace just days after elections, a familiar scene in the politically volatile West African nation. Incumbent President Embalo and rival Dias have both claimed victory, though the main opposition was barred from the vote. This instability fuels the country's role as a drug transit hub.

item.title: Trump's pardons, Ozempic, and cheaper turkey: Unpacking Thanskgiving 2025
item.description: But this year, the performance feels different. The pardon stands on one end of the cultural table, loud and ceremonial, while the rest of Thanksgiving sits on the other end, quieter and lighter than before. Turkeys are cheaper, appetites are shrinking, and the national feast is no longer quite the binge it once was. Somehow, everything around the ritual has changed, and the ritual itself has stayed exactly the same — which might be the most American thing about it.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
